verdict.rationale: First-party docs claim Parse turns 'the most complex layouts, tables' into clean markdown, and that every table can be pulled into pandas DataFrames with source-page provenance. That establishes general table-to-structure output, and one community user praised results on a complex layout. However, no evidence specifically covers merged cells, nested headers, multi-page table stitching or HTML table output. One hands-on user reported that table numbers 'didn't appear to be in tabular format', but this was hedged interface confusion rather than a concrete documented failure. Missing for 10: documented handling of merged cells and nested/multi-level headers, multi-page table continuation, HTML table output option, independent corroboration of structural fidelity on complex tables.

support.subject: As a data engineer, complex tables — merged cells, nested headers, multi-page spans — come out as faithful HTML/markdown structure

citations.quote: Turn even the most complex layouts, tables, charts, handwriting, checkboxes, and images into clean markdown
pull every table out into pandas DataFrames with source-page provenance
